title: The Silent Hunters: Owls
intro: You should spend about 20 minutes on this passage.

paras.t: Owls have fascinated people for thousands of years. In some cultures they are symbols of wisdom, while in others they are signs of bad luck, and they appear in stories from ancient Greece to modern children's books. There are over two hundred species, found on every continent except Antarctica, from tiny owls the size of a sparrow to great horned owls that can carry off a rabbit. What unites them is the way they hunt: silently, at night, using senses that are among the most remarkable in the animal kingdom. This passage explains how the bodies of owls are adapted to their way of life.

The first adaptation is vision. An owl's eyes are huge in proportion to its head: if human eyes were the same relative size, they would be as big as grapefruits. Their shape is tubular, rather like a pair of binoculars, and this gives excellent sight in dim light, because a large lens gathers more light. The price is that the eyes are fixed in their sockets and cannot move. An owl must turn its whole head to look around. To do this, it has fourteen neck bones, twice as many as a human, and can rotate its head up to two hundred and seventy degrees in either direction.

The second adaptation is hearing. In many species, the face is a flat disc of feathers, shaped like a dish, which collects sound and directs it to the ears. The ears themselves are placed at slightly different heights on the sides of the head, so that a sound reaches one ear a fraction of a second before the other, and the owl can work out exactly where it came from, both left and right and up and down. A barn owl can catch a mouse in total darkness by sound alone, in conditions in which it could not see its prey at all.

The third adaptation is silent flight. Most birds make a swishing noise as their wings beat the air, but owls glide almost without a sound. The leading edge of their main wing feathers has a comb-like fringe, which breaks up the flow of air into small streams and reduces turbulence. The upper surface of the feathers is covered with a soft down, like velvet, and the trailing edge is fringed. As a result, the prey does not hear the owl approaching, and the owl, in turn, can listen for its prey without the noise of its own wings. Engineers have studied these feathers in order to design quieter fans and aircraft.

Owls are carnivores, feeding mainly on small mammals, such as mice and voles, but also on insects, fish and birds. Some species can take surprisingly large prey. The hunting method is usually to wait on a perch and listen, then swoop down on the target with talons spread. Owls swallow small prey whole, and since they cannot digest the bones, fur or feathers, they cough these up some hours later in the form of a compact pellet. Scientists collect and dissect the pellets to learn what the owl has eaten, and from this they can measure the numbers of small mammals in an area.

Most owls nest in holes in trees, old buildings or abandoned nests of other birds, and some, like the burrowing owl, nest underground. The female lays between two and eight eggs, depending on the species and the supply of food. In years when mice and voles are plentiful, owls may raise large broods; in lean years, they may not breed at all. The chicks are covered in white down and are fed by both parents. They leave the nest after about five to ten weeks but depend on their parents for food for some time afterwards. Many young owls die in their first winter.

Some owl species are in trouble. The destruction of forests and old trees removes nesting sites, and poisons used to kill rats and mice can pass up the food chain to the owls that eat them. Dr Rosa Lindgren, a conservation biologist, has shown that putting up nest boxes in farmland can double the number of barn owls in an area within a few years, and that the owls in turn reduce the number of rodents which damage crops. Farmers who put up boxes, she says, get free pest control. Her work is a reminder that, in nature, even the creature that works at night can help us in the day.
